bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.title: List the nonresidues
bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.body:
The squares mod $29$ are $1,4,5,6,7,9,13,16,20,22,23,24,25,28$, so the nonresidues are $2,3,8,10,11,12,14,15,17,18,19,21,26,27$ ($14$ of them; $0$ is a square, so it is not a nonresidue).

With $a,b\in\{1,\dots,28\}$ and $a+b\equiv1\pmod{29}$ we need $a+b=30$. Checking each nonresidue $a$ for $30-a$: $3\leftrightarrow27$, $11\leftrightarrow19$, $12\leftrightarrow18$, $15\leftrightarrow15$ are all nonresidue pairs. Ordered pairs: $(3,27),(27,3),(11,19),(19,11),(12,18),(18,12),(15,15)$, i.e. $7$.

**Answer: 7**

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.title: Character sum
bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.body:
Since $29\equiv1\pmod4$, $-1$ is a residue, so $a$ is a nonresidue iff $-a$ is. Setting $a'=-a$, the pairs become consecutive nonresidues $(a',a'+1)$, and for a prime $p\equiv1\pmod 4$ there are exactly $\frac{p-1}4=7$ such pairs.

**Answer: 7**

bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.title: A multiplicative function on F_121
bmt-2018-spring-number-theory-tiebreaker.body:
The rule says $f(x+iy)$ is multiplicative in the Gaussian integers, and by periodicity $f$ is defined on $\mathbb Z[i]/(11)\cong\mathbb F_{121}$ ($11\equiv3\pmod4$, so $x^2+1$ is irreducible mod $11$). Multiplicativity gives $f(1,0)^2=f(1,0)$ so $f(1,0)\in\{0,1\}$.

If $f(1,0)=0$ then $f\equiv0$ and $f(1,1)=0$. If $f(1,0)=1$ then $f$ restricted to the cyclic group $\mathbb F_{121}^*$ (order $120$) is a character $\chi$ (and $f(0,0)$ is $0$, or $f\equiv1$ which is the trivial character). The value $\chi(1+i)$ can be any $m$th root of unity where $m$ is the multiplicative order of $1+i$, and every such value occurs for some character.

The order of $1+i$: $(1+i)^2=2i$, $(1+i)^8=(2i)^4=16\equiv5$, which has order $5$ mod $11$, so $(1+i)^{40}=1$ and $(1+i)^{20}=(2i)^{10}=2^{10}\cdot i^{10}=-1\ne1$, $(1+i)^8\ne1$. The order divides $40$, does not divide $20$ or $8$, so it is $40$.

So $f(1,1)$ takes one of the $40$ values $\zeta$ with $\zeta^{40}=1$, or $0$: $41$ possibilities.

**Answer: 41**
